\documentclass{amsart}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\newtheorem{corollary}[theorem]{Corollary}
\newtheorem{claim}{Claim}
\theoremstyle{definition}\newtheorem{definition}[theorem]{Definition}
\newtheorem*{remark*}{Remark}
\begin{document}
\section{One}
\begin{definition}\label{def:a}A definition.\end{definition}
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:a}A lemma.\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}Uses Definition~\ref{def:a}.\end{proof}
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:a}A theorem.\end{theorem}
\begin{claim}\label{cl:a}An independent counter.\end{claim}
\section{Two}
\subsection{Two point one}
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:b}Counter reset by section.\end{lemma}
\begin{remark*}Unnumbered.\end{remark*}
\begin{claim}\label{cl:b}Not reset.\end{claim}
\begin{corollary}\label{cor:b}Shares the theorem counter.\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:a}]
Combine Lemma~\ref{lem:a} and \cref{lem:b,cl:a}.
\begin{claim}\label{cl:inner}Nested.\end{claim}
\begin{proof}Inner proof cites Corollary~\ref{cor:b}.\end{proof}
\end{proof}
\appendix
\section{Extra}
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:app}In the appendix.\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:a}.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
